correctness.rationale: For any scale 0<=lambda<=3, the four exact normalized Hermite derivatives (6t(1-t), 3(1-t)^2, 3t^2, 3(1-2t)^2) are nonnegative, yielding one-input BV equality. Each minmod region maps input first differences linearly to cubics. The step-column central cell has BV 1 and each selected neighboring endpoint hump U or W has BV 8 lambda/27, giving 1+8 lambda min(2,n-2)/27. Straight-line integration handles changes of selector region. The explicit secant families (1,2) for n=3 and (2,1,2,...) for n>=4 with a 1/4 step perturbation attain the bound. For lambda outside [0,3], data 0,1,2 cause a sign reversal of the first cubic derivative. The included checker verifies exact corner and step identities plus numeric-variation witnesses, without treating finite tests as all-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The minmod Hermite cubic is a standard shape-preserving smooth reconstruction, whose one-input monotonicity does not quantify error propagation between two data sets. The exact dimension-sensitive 35/27 and 43/27 stability factors quantify this missing stability property. The proof identifies the 8/27 cubic hump as the structural mechanism, gives attaining perturbations and the maximal variation-preserving slope interval, furnishing reproducible benchmarks for stable C1 interpolants and a comparison with discontinuous cellwise-limited reconstruction.
